([[High Point, North Carolina]]) | college = [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]] (2018–2021) | highlights = * [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] Sixth Man of the Year (2020) | medal_templates = }} '''Aaron Wiggins''' (born January 2, 1999) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland Terrapins]]. ==Early life and high school career== Wiggins grew up playing basketball and [[American football|football]] and running [[track and field|track]]. Through his childhood, he played the [[piano]] and [[trombone]], acted in plays and danced.{{cite web |last1=Giambalvo |first1=Emily |title=Maryland's Aaron Wiggins knows tap, jazz, ballet and hip-hop. Up next is the Big Dance. |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2019/02/26/marylands-aaron-wiggins-knows-tap-jazz-ballet-hip-hop-up-next-is-big-dance/ |website=[[The Washington Post]] |accessdate=August 14, 2020 |date=February 26, 2019}} Wiggins played basketball for [[Grimsley High School]] in [[Greensboro, North Carolina]] before transferring to [[Wesleyan Christian Academy]] in [[High Point, North Carolina]].{{cite web |last1=Bendel |first1=Jeff |last2=Shaw |first2=Jamie |title=Is Aaron Wiggins the Big Ten's Most Lethal Shooter in 2019-20?! |url=https://phenomhoopreport.com/is-aaron-wiggins-the-big-tens-most-lethal-shooter-in-2019-20/ |publisher=Phenom Hoop Report |accessdate=August 14, 2020 |date=September 3, 2019}} As a senior, he was an NCISAA Class 3A All-State selection.{{cite web |last1=Wertz Jr. |first1=Langston |title=Area players honored on NCISAA all-state basketball teams |url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/high-school/article202298044.html |website=[[The Charlotte Observer]] |accessdate=August 14, 2020 |date=February 26, 2018}} Wiggins competed for Team Charlotte on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] circuit.{{cite web |last1=Kendziora |first1=Thomas |title=Aaron Wiggins Poised To Make Sophomore Leap For Maryland Men's Basketball |url=https://pressboxonline.com/2019/11/27/aaron-wiggins-poised-to-make-sophomore-leap-for-maryland-mens-basketball/ |website=PressBox |accessdate=August 14, 2020 |date=November 27, 2019}} A consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to play college basketball for [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]] on June 3, 2017.{{cite web |last1=Markus |first1=Don |title=Rising four-star small forward recruit Aaron Wiggins commits to Maryland |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/terps/bal-rising-small-forward-recruit-aaron-wiggins-taking-official-visit-to-maryland-20170603-story.html |website=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |accessdate=August 14, 2020 |date=June 3, 2017}} He had drawn the attention of Maryland's coaching staff while they were visiting Wesleyan to watch his teammate [[Jaylen Hoard]]. ==College career== Wiggins began his freshman season as a starter, but later told coach [[Mark Turgeon]] that he was more comfortable coming off the bench. As a freshman at Maryland, he played the most minutes among his team's reserves.{{cite web |last1=DuBose |first1=Brooks |title=Maryland Basketball's Aaron Wiggins A Bench Player In Name Only |url=https://pressboxonline.com/2019/02/19/maryland-basketballs-aaron-wiggins-a-bench-player-in-name-only/ |website=PressBox |accessdate=August 14, 2020 |date=February 19, 2019}} He led Maryland with a season-high 15 points in losses to [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] and [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]].{{cite web |last1=Markus |first1=Don |title=Staying aggressive has made freshman Aaron Wiggins a road warrior for Maryland |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/terps/bs-sp-wiggins-maryland-basketball-road-0218-story.html |website=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |accessdate=August 14, 2020 |date=February 19, 2019}} He finished the season averaging 8.3 points and 3.3 rebounds in 23.5 minutes per game, shooting a team-high 41.3 percent from three-point range.{{cite web |last1=Giambalvo |first1=Emily |title=Aaron Wiggins has become stronger and more confident, but Maryland wants more |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2019/11/15/aaron-wiggins-has-become-stronger-more-confident-maryland-wants-more/ |website=[[The Washington Post]] |accessdate=August 14, 2020 |date=November 15, 2019}}{{cite web |last1=Markus |first1=Don |title=As sophomore year begins, Maryland wing Aaron Wiggins has seen his game and confidence grow |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/terps/bs-sp-maryland-basketball-aaron-wiggins-20191031-qjnsfsddy5dxtdturwhlps6fxy-story.html |website=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |accessdate=August 14, 2020 |date=October 31, 2019}} On February 23, 2020, Wiggins scored a sophomore season-high 20 points, recording six three-pointers, in a 79–72 loss to [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]].{{cite web |last1=Gold |first1=Jordan |title=TT Court Vision: Aaron Wiggins shines but Terps falter at Ohio State |url=https://www.testudotimes.com/maryland-terps-basketball/2020/2/25/21151180/film-room-breakdown-maryland-mens-basketball-at-ohio-state-best-worst-plays-loss-aaron-wiggins |publisher=Testudo Times |accessdate=August 14, 2020 |date=February 25, 2020}} As a sophomore, he averaged 10.4 points, 4.9 rebounds and 1.4 assists per game and was named [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] Sixth Man of the Year.{{cite web |last1=Oyefusi |first1=Daniel |title=Maryland basketball's Anthony Cowan Jr., Jalen Smith earn All-Big Ten honors |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/terps/bs-sp-cowan-smith-big-ten-maryland-mens-basketball-20200309-t2c2ppvchzb5toc7hwj25u32we-story.html |website=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |accessdate=August 14, 2020 |date=March 9, 2020}} In the final game of his junior season, Wiggins scored a career-high 27 points in a 96–77 loss to [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] at the second round of the [[2021 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]].{{cite web |last1=Steinberg |first1=Jacob |title=What Does Aaron Wiggins’ Decision To Leave Mean For Maryland Men’s Basketball? |url=https://pressboxonline.com/2021/07/06/what-does-aaron-wiggins-decision-to-leave-mean-for-maryland-mens-basketball/ |website=PressBox |access-date=July 26, 2021 |date=July 6, 2021}} As a junior, he averaged 14.5 points, 5.8 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game, earning All-Big Ten honorable mention. On April 9, 2021, Wiggins declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite web |last1=Giambalvo |first1=Emily |title=Maryland’s Aaron Wiggins, Eric Ayala declare for NBA draft while maintaining eligibility |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2021/04/09/aaron-wiggins-nba-draft/ |website=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=July 26, 2021 |date=April 9, 2021}} He later decided to remain in the draft.{{cite web |last1=Oyefusi |first1=Daniel |title=Maryland guard Aaron Wiggins keeping name in NBA draft, will forgo senior season |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/terps/bs-sp-maryland-aaron-wiggins-nba-draft-20210705-jhl6ufsqazfmxjrszicgxhrmf4-story.html |website=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |access-date=July 26, 2021
